description: Registry-published RDAP services for TLDs missing from the IANA RDAP bootstrap. Each base URL is checked live with one random 24-character label (see live-validation.json); source names the registry documentation. The IANA bootstrap wins when it lists the TLD.

routes.notes: SWITCH documents 404 as "usually" not registered but "that doesn't always mean that the domain name can be registered", 200 as "registered and/or cannot be registered at this time", and 429 as access restricted. Port-43 WHOIS refuses many clients and is not used.
Same SWITCH service and status semantics as .ch: a 404 is usually, not always, a registrable name; a 200 can also mean the name cannot be registered now.

The .CO Registrar Guide (January 2026) documents RDAP (429 rate limiting, HEAD checks) but prints no base URL. This base URL is on the registry's own domain; it was posted by a forum member on 2025-10-18, and a CentralNic reply relayed in the same thread on 2025-10-20 said adding the server to the IANA bootstrap was still to be done after the migration (https://www.namepros.com/threads/the-queried-object-does-not-exist-domain-not-found-for-co-warning.1366138/). The guide advises against WHOIS for availability checks, so WHOIS is not used.
